item.title: Hip Hop Caucus Makes Final 2026 Midterm Push
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Hip Hop Caucus is pressing young voters to turn cultural influence into votes as its Respect My Vote campaign turns 18.
item.content:encoded:
Hip Hop Caucus is pressing young voters to use their cultural influence in the final days before the November 3 midterm elections.

The group’s president and CEO, Rev. Lennox Yearwood Jr., told The Washington Informer, “What I want this generation to understand is that this is your fight more than ever.”

The nonpartisan Respect My Vote campaign marked its 18th anniversary on July 28. In its 2026 announcement, the group set goals of reaching 20 million people, bringing 500,000 voters to the polls and making 4.5 million voter contacts. It also aimed for 175,000 combined online voter registrations, pledges and registration checks. Those targets covered work through media, partnerships, events, training and digital outreach. The campaign focuses on Gen Z and Millennial voters.

The group is also part of a wider push for voter education. Word In Black’s “Know Before You Vote” event page now offers a replay and lists Hip Hop Caucus digital and production associate director JaRel Clay among its panelists. The discussion covered voter engagement, key issues and the power of the Black vote. Word In Black head of content Joseph Williams served as moderator.

The link between artists and voter education has been part of the group’s work for years. In 2008, T.I. joined its voter registration effort, with a launch planned at Washington, D.C.’s 9:30 Club. The free event was set to bring celebrities and the public together for a discussion about young people taking part in civic life. Its rollout also included DJ Green Lantern and shirts from T.I.’s AKOO clothing line.

By 2012, 2 Chainz had become a Respect My Vote spokesman. The message included voting rights for people with felony records. Organizers also sought new registrations and participation from adults ages 18 to 40. His own experience was central to the message: the rapper said learning he could vote mattered to him after his felony conviction. Yearwood said the group chose 2 Chainz because he could speak to that audience in an authentic way.

Now, Yearwood sees social media giving students and celebrities a way to reach followers. He said the group would keep organizing after Election Day.

item.title: Kim Kardashian’s Exoneration Support Draws Objections
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Kim Kardashian's support for Stacey Tyler's exoneration campaign drew objections from the children of the woman he was convicted of killing.
item.content:encoded:
The children of Mary “Evon” Jennings Fleetwood challenged the exoneration campaign Kim Kardashian amplified for Stacey “Sabur” Tyler, saying their mother’s voice mattered, according to Capital B.

Patrice “Monique” Jennings and brothers Darius and Jermaine told the outlet they believed Tyler’s murder conviction was correct.

“She’s not here to fight for herself,” Monique told Capital B. “So I have to.”

Fleetwood suffered fatal burns on November 5, 1993 and died 15 days later. In 1995, her boyfriend, Stacey Anthony Tyler, received a death sentence after a jury convicted him of first-degree murder.

The North Carolina Supreme Court upheld the conviction and sentence on June 6, 1997. Its opinion described testimony that Tyler had abused Fleetwood and threatened to burn her home with her children inside.

Tyler presented no evidence during the guilt phase. At sentencing, he denied attacking Fleetwood or setting her on fire and testified that he tried to extinguish the flames.

The opinion also detailed Fleetwood’s changing account. She initially indicated Tyler hadn’t burned her. After being told he was in custody and couldn’t hurt her, she answered further questions with nods identifying him as her attacker, according to testimony reviewed by the court.

The Making an Exoneree campaign offered a different account in its description of “I Dare Not Dream,” a film about Tyler. The group maintained that a kerosene heater caused an accident, challenged the reliability of prosecution witnesses and denied a history of abuse.

Making an Exoneree began at Georgetown University in 2018. The program combines investigations with films and campaigns seeking release. Its undergraduate teams gather material through prison visits and trips to the locations involved in cases. Georgetown Law students assist those teams while also working with lawyers pursuing relief for incarcerated people.

Kardashian has brought criminal justice stories to entertainment audiences elsewhere. She joined the producing team for “The Fear of 13,” the Broadway play about Nick Yarris’ wrongful conviction starring Adrien Brody and Tessa Thompson.

Monique said Kardashian’s June post introduced her to Tyler’s campaign. She said the filmmakers hadn’t contacted her beforehand.

Making an Exoneree told Capital B its films expressed its evidence assessment. It said it generally avoided contacting victims’ families out of concern for their trauma. It stood by its advocacy.

item.title: BBC Sets UK Rap Chart Countdown
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: BBC Radio 1Xtra will air the Official UK Rap Chart with Kenny Allstar, with the first countdown set for November 6.
item.content:encoded:
BBC Radio 1Xtra is putting British rap’s weekly chart race on the air, with Kenny Allstar hosting the first Official UK Rap Chart countdown on November 6.

The ranking will combine UK sales and streams for eligible UK rap singles, Official Charts announced. Allstar will reveal it during his Friday show, which airs from 9 p.m. to 11 p.m. UK time.

“For me, this has been a long time coming,” Allstar said.

UK rap had already left its mark on the country’s wider singles chart years before this dedicated ranking. Dave and Central Cee released “Sprinter” on June 1, 2023, as the lead single from their joint EP, Split Decision.

That first chart week brought 108,200 units and 13.4 million streams. The streaming total set a new weekly high for a rap song on the UK chart at the time. By its fifth week at No. 1, the pair had passed the runs of Dave’s “Starlight” and Dizzee Rascal’s “Dance Wiv Me,” as AllHipHop reported. It showed how far a British rap collaboration could travel in a chart shared with the biggest pop releases.

The album chart told a similar story that summer. D-Block Europe reached No. 6 with DBE World, released July 7, 2023. It gave the South London duo a seventh UK Top 10 album, which was the most for a British rap act at that point.

The Streets had six Top 10 albums and Bugzy Malone had five. D-Block Europe’s earlier Top 10 entries included Home Alone at No. 6 in 2019 and PTSD at No. 4 that same year. Lap 5 peaked at No. 2 in 2022.

By the end of 2023, the full “Sprinter” run had stretched to 10 consecutive weeks at No. 1, from June to August. Beyond Britain, its Spotify tally had topped half a billion plays by that December, according to British GQ. In its December 19 report, GQ also listed it as Spotify’s most-streamed song in the UK for 2023. The track also generated 900,000 TikTok creations in its first two months, a separate sign of how listeners were using the song beyond the charts.

Fans can check the new ranking at OfficialCharts.com each Friday alongside Allstar’s radio countdown.

item.title: Mariah Carey Teases Grunge Album With “#notyet” Reply
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Mariah Carey gave fans a new grunge album hint on Reddit, revisiting the unreleased lead vocals behind her 1995 rock project.
item.content:encoded:
Mariah Carey answered another call for her unreleased grunge album with a new hint during her Reddit “Ask Me Anything” on Friday, October 30.

“I get asked this about once a week,” she wrote when a fan asked about the album. “my answer is…#notyet (this is a hint!)”

The reply left the timing open. Carey gave no release date for her version of Someone’s Ugly Daughter, the rock project she made while recording Daydream in 1995.

A version of that album already came out under the name Chick, with her friend Clarissa Dane on lead vocals. The recordings fans have been asking Carey to release feature Carey singing lead. She discussed the secret project in her 2020 memoir.

That difference goes back to the label pressure around the record. As AllHipHop previously reported, executives worried about what the rock detour would do to her mainstream image. Carey recorded her original leads as “D. Sue,” then took a background vocal role.

The music gave her room to work outside those limits. On “Las Culturistas” in 2024, she described the sessions in terms of the freedom she lacked elsewhere in her career.

“I had no freedom during that time. That was my freedom,” Carey said during that earlier interview with Matt Rogers and Bowen Yang.

She also told the hosts, “You will hear it,” while asking who could help put the album out. The question of recovering her original vocals had come up before: in a 2022 “Rolling Stone Music Now” interview, she discussed recordings that had been shelved and still needed to be found.

Friday’s Reddit conversation took place around a different visit to her archives. Her first AMA in r/popculturechat was set for 3:27 P.M. Eastern and marked the 25th anniversary of Glitter. The expanded digital edition arrived that day with 15 additional tracks, while the album returned to vinyl for the first time since 2001.

Those additions included a 1997 version of “Lead The Way,” a Carey-only version of “Want You” and a rough demo of “Never Too Far.” The anniversary collection also included new collaborations with Channel Tres and Rochelle Jordan.

item.title: Violent J Rejects Family Era Reunion
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Violent J rejected a paid Family Era reunion with former collaborators as Insane Clown Posse prepared for Michigan Halloween shows.
item.content:encoded:
Violent J ruled out a Family Era reunion as Insane Clown Posse prepared for Halloween shows in Michigan.

Asked by Metro Times about a Family Era show with Twiztid, ABK and Blaze, he rejected a paid reunion.

“There’s nothing, no amount of money, that would get me to get onstage with those guys,” he said.

The interview was published October 28. He called the split a betrayal. His only suggested exception was hypothetical: ending world hunger.

Twiztid’s Jamie Madrox and Monoxide came out of House of Krazees. Violent J liked a demo they made after that trio broke up and signed them to Psychopathic Records. That run included the 2009 album W.I.C.K.E.D., which reached No. 11 on the Billboard 200 chart.

In a 2011 interview with The Village Voice, Madrox credited ICP with taking time to teach the duo and help sharpen their music. Monoxide said they spent years learning from the group. Madrox said that even without Psychopathic, he believed Twiztid would still have pursued music. What the label had changed, in his view, was the reach of that career and the doors that opened.

Madrox described a bond built on trust and years of work. Monoxide said ICP came to respect their business skills as well as their music. The duo also recalled ICP encouraging them to use face paint, after they had worried about taking the group’s look.

Twiztid later left Psychopathic. AllHipHop’s 2014 Halloween feature identified Abominationz as the duo’s final release for the label. In 2015, Twiztid put out its first album through its own Majik Ninja Entertainment, according to CityBeat.

For this year’s holiday run, the group’s publicist announced three Michigan dates: October 29 and October 30 at The Vault in Saginaw, followed by October 31 at Detroit’s Masonic Temple. The announcement described the Saginaw bookings as ICP’s first concerts in that city. It listed the October 29 show as sold out when the release was issued.

The Detroit date is billed as the 33rd annual Hallowicked Clown Show. Along with ICP, the announced music lineup includes Ouija Macc, Wakko The Kidd, Diggy Graves, Ganksta N-I-P and Klokwerk E.

item.title: Janelle Monáe, Lizzo & Maino Deliver Standout Halloween Looks
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Halloween 2026 gave celebrities a chance to show out and fans a welcome break from reality. Here are some of our favorite looks.
item.content:encoded:
Halloween stopped being just for children and the Comic-Con crowd a long time ago. These days, everybody wants in, and celebrities have turned the holiday into an unofficial competition of creativity, comedy and who has entirely too much money to spend on a costume.

This year brought plenty of all three. From Maino’s impersonation of 50 Cent to Janelle Monáe’s hyperrealistic monster creation and Lizzo’s homage to the late, great Dolly Parton, the looks gave fans plenty to laugh at, admire and debate. Some went for nostalgia. Others went for shock value. And a few clearly had professional teams working overtime.

But underneath the makeup, masks and elaborate reveals, Halloween offers something people could use right now: a little relief.

Look around. Between the headlines, the bills, the political chaos and the everyday pressure of keeping your life together, reality already feels like a dysfunctional dystopian movie. At least on Halloween, we get to choose our monsters.

For one night, people can trade their problems for a costume, get a little ridiculous and remember that having fun is still allowed. The world doesn’t stop being messy, but there’s something refreshing about watching people put this much effort into making each other smile.

Here are some of the best celebrity Halloween looks of 2026.

Janelle Monae 👀

Joey Bada$$ as Slick Rick 

Tyga

Justina Valentine 

Affion Crockett

DJ Diamond Kutz as the goat rocker Tina Turner

iShowSpeed evokes Miles Morales aka Spider-Man

G Herbo and the Fam as The Jacksons

Lizzo honors Dolly Parton

Luda and wife as Prince and Apollonia

Doechii gives the living icon Grace Jones her flowers

Maino trolls 50 Cent yet again

The Game did Ghostface sitting in the Mercedes Benz SLR Stirling Moss

Who did we miss? Add them in the comments!

item.title: Gnarls Barkley Cancels November Tour As Ticket Buyers Await Refunds
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Gnarls Barkley canceled its November tour ahead of the San Francisco opener, with ticket buyers due refunds within 14 to 21 days.
item.content:encoded:
Gnarls Barkley canceled its November “To Whom It Still Concerns Tour” ahead of the November 5 opening show at The Masonic in San Francisco.

Ticket buyers are due refunds. The Ticketmaster notice for the San Francisco opener says customers do not need to take action. Pollstar reported that Ticketmaster notified buyers to expect their money within 14 to 21 days.

The reason for the cancellation remains unclear. The San Francisco Chronicle reported that neither Gnarls Barkley nor promoter Live Nation had publicly explained the decision.

Live Nation announced the outing September 18 as a nine-city North American tour, advertising the first Gnarls Barkley tour in 18 years. But the name on the bill did not mean both members would be onstage.

Danger Mouse’s representative had already said the producer never planned to join the shows, according to the Chronicle. CeeLo Green had his partner’s permission to use the group’s name for the performances, the representative said. That clarification preceded the cancellation.

The live plans followed a recording reunion. Atlanta was billed as the pair’s third and final album, with AllHipHop previously reporting a 13-track project led by “Pictures.” The album was announced for a March 6, 2026 release through 10k Projects and Atlantic Records. Their previous album, The Odd Couple, came out in 2008. “Pictures” drew on Green’s memories of riding Atlanta trains alone after his middle school principal sent him home early on Fridays.

The canceled November schedule reached well beyond the opening night. Ticketmaster’s listings mark the November 7 show at Los Angeles’ Wiltern and November 10 stop at Atlanta’s Coca-Cola Roxy as canceled. The same status appears for Detroit on November 13, Boston on November 15 and Silver Spring, Maryland on November 19. Ticketmaster’s lineups list Gallant for the first four stops and Duckwrth for the remaining November dates.

Toronto’s HISTORY show on November 22 is also canceled. In New York, Ticketmaster lists canceled Irving Plaza dates for both November 24 and November 25, adding a second night beyond the original announcement’s itinerary. The planned November 28 finale at Chicago’s House of Blues is marked canceled as well.

item.title: YG Confronts Himself
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: YG examined the choices behind his family, street and business troubles while discussing personal change with Boardroom.
item.content:encoded:
YG tied family, street and business problems to his own behavior while discussing his effort to change with Damien Scott on Boardroom‘s “On Record.”

“I realized a lot of my issues and problems come from within. Self-inflicted.”

That struggle had already shaped The Gentlemen’s Club, as GQ described. On “Hitman,” the target turned out to be YG himself. Songs including “Ready to Die” and “Insecure” put his doubts into the music, making his own state of mind central to the record’s plot.

The magazine’s account of his June show at West Hollywood’s Roxy Theater described a performance of the full album with YG and his crew in suits. Fans had been asked to dress up too. Onstage, he discussed feeling overlooked and being pushed by people close to him to improve.

His guests kept the West Coast connections in place. Shoreline Mafia joined “Hollywood,” while Tyler, The Creator appeared on “On the Low.” Pusha T teamed with him for “OMG.” The personal material sat alongside those collaborations.

Released June 19, 2026, The Gentlemen’s Club ran 15 songs and 54 minutes, according to Apple Music’s catalog. The credits listed 4Hunnid Music under an exclusive license to 10K Projects. That followed the Def Jam period that ended with 2022’s I Got Issues, then a joint project with Tyga and another entry in his Just Re’d Up mixtape series.

That was a change from the Def Jam rollout for My Krazy Life in 2014. AllHipHop covered the album’s Atlanta listening session at Patchwerk Studios in 2014, when Def Jam played it for DJs, executives and media ahead of its March 18 release.

Jeezy and DJ Mustard explained the work behind the project at that event and compared it to Dr. Dre’s The Chronic.

The new album also got a stage rollout. The July 21, 2026 announcement for “The Gentlemen’s Club Tour” mapped out 19 cities, starting September 10 in Boston and ending November 7 in Honolulu. Mozzy and Chef Boy were named as support, with Kalan.FrFr and Natalie Nunn on select dates. The announced route included a Los Angeles show at Crypto.com Arena.

item.title: Timbaland Sues Ex-Managers For $15 Million After Foreclosure Scare
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Timbaland sought $15 million from former managers, alleging unpaid bills, excess commissions and damage to his business ventures.
item.content:encoded:
Timbaland sought $15 million from former manager Gary Marella and business manager Bruce Seckendorf, accusing them of draining his finances while his mortgage went unpaid.

According to The Hollywood Reporter, he filed the 65-page complaint October 30 in Los Angeles Superior Court. The claims included fraud, civil theft and breach of fiduciary duty.

Timbaland alleged a 2025 foreclosure notice exposed the problems, including unpaid federal taxes and penalties. He accused Marella of taking excess commissions from “Verzuz” payments and his catalog sale, plus mismanaging their Beatclub venture.

THR detailed allegations that Marella took $500,000 extra on each of two $5 million “Verzuz” payments and $775,000 above his stated 10 percent catalog-sale commission.

“The foreclosure was not caused simply because Plaintiffs had no money,” the complaint said, according to THR.

Mono Music Group, LL Business Management and Seckendorf Hasson Reilly & Kobay CPA’s were also named. THR reported that neither man nor their firms immediately responded to its comment requests. The report said both men were fired in 2025.

The catalog sale involved years of Timbaland’s work. Hipgnosis announced the purchase in October 2019, describing a collection of 108 albums and songs. Its announcement included work recorded by Aaliyah, Jay-Z, Missy Elliott and Justin Timberlake. Marella appeared in that announcement as Timbaland’s manager and welcomed the agreement.

Beatclub grew from another idea the two men pursued together. In a 2021 Associated Press interview, Timbaland described calling Marella with his plan for a marketplace that could help lesser-known creators reach established artists.

The proposed model let members set prices and retain their music rights, revenue and publishing royalties. Timbaland also framed the venture as a way to learn the business side of music.

“You’re learning financial literacy,” he told AP at the time.

Marella told AP he backed the idea immediately. Justin Timberlake had joined and said Timbaland was already introducing him to collaborators through Beatclub.

“Verzuz” also had its own history of payment disputes. AllHipHop reported in March 2024 that Timbaland and Swizz Beatz sought unpaid attorney’s fees from Triller following a settlement over the platform. That action concerned Triller’s obligations under their agreement.

item.title: Joe Budden Plays Big Switty In “Law & Order” Murder Plot
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Joe Budden played rapper Big Switty in "Law & Order," where a $300,000 mask deal put his character in a murder investigation.
item.content:encoded:
Joe Budden entered a fictional murder investigation as rapper Big Switty in “Law & Order,” with a $300,000 art deal at the center of his character’s dispute.

His guest appearance came in “Property,” the fourth episode of Season 26, which aired October 29. The episode followed the murder of an antiquities dealer, according to TVmaze’s episode listing.

The cameo followed a real business connection with Wolf Entertainment, the company behind “Law & Order.” Budden had become the host of “Crime in America,” a true crime podcast from Wolf Entertainment, Headline Studio and Budden. Advance Local’s announcement said the first episode debuted August 11, less than three months before his television appearance.

The podcast put him in conversation with local journalists who had been reporting on cases in their own communities. Those interviews drew on Advance Local’s network of reporters across the country. Its stated focus covered both developing crimes and cases those reporters had followed for years. That gave the series room for stories gaining national attention as well as ones that had yet to reach a wider audience.

Headline Studio described an approach built around what had happened, who had been affected and what remained unknown. Its rollout called for new episodes on Tuesdays.

On the scripted show, Switty told detectives that an Egyptian mask he had bought was fake and he wanted his money back, according to Billboard. He said he had been having dinner with his manager and lawyer at 9:30 p.m. the previous night. A threatening voicemail to art broker Andrew Carson brought the character into their investigation.

The show’s way of telling a story had figured in Budden’s music long before this guest spot. In an August 2008 AllHipHop interview, he discussed the song “Who” and his effort to trace changes in Hip-Hop.

Budden said he had wanted to make that kind of record for some time. He explained that he wanted listeners to follow how things began and how the culture changed. He also said he kept the beat simple so it would leave room for what he was saying. The television reference was explicit: “I wanted to do it like a Law & Order episode.”
